title: Coral stitch
subtitle: A knotted outline stitch that ties small raised knots along a line
excerpt: Coral stitch builds a textured line by forming a small knot at regular intervals along the stitching path. The thread lies along the line, a short bite of fabric is caught under a loop, and pulling through locks a firm knot in place. It works well for outlines, stems, and any line that needs a broken, beaded quality.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), knotted outline stitches chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), coral stitch entry.

content.text: Coral stitch works right to left along a drawn line, or top to bottom on a vertical line. The working thread lies flat along the line ahead of the needle. At each knot position, the needle dips into the fabric slightly to the right of the thread and comes back up slightly to the left, with the thread looped under the needle tip. Pulling through traps the loop and seats a small raised knot on the surface.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton 2 to 3 strands, or perle 8 for a crisper knot

content.text: Secure the thread on the back and bring it up at (A), the right-hand end of the line. Lay the thread flat along the line to the left.

At the first knot position, insert the needle at (B), a small distance to the right of the laid thread and slightly below the line. Bring the needle tip up at (C), a small distance to the left of the thread and on the line. Do not pull through yet.
Loop the working thread under the needle tip, from left to right. The thread forms a U-shape beneath the needle.
Pull the needle and thread through, drawing steadily until the knot tightens snugly on the fabric surface. Do not pull so hard that the knot collapses flat.
Lay the thread along the line again toward the next knot position and repeat from step 2. Keep the spacing between knots consistent throughout the line.

items.symptom: The knot will not form and the thread slides through
items.cause: The working thread was not looped under the needle tip before pulling through.
items.fix: Pause after inserting the needle at (B) and bringing it up at (C). Check the thread passes under the needle tip before you pull. Slow the motion until the habit is set.

items.symptom: The knots pull flat or sink into the fabric
items.cause: Too much tension when pulling through, or the bite of fabric between (B) and (C) is too small to hold the knot.
items.fix: Take a slightly larger bite of fabric. Pull gently and stop as soon as the knot sits on the surface.
